subject: Compliance lighthouse: pre-audit questions & FedRAMP path
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Adams <claire@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Compliance lighthouse: pre-audit questions & FedRAMP path

Team — forwarding a short list of clarifying questions that came up in today's board pre-brief with Acme. We need crisp answers so the auditor intake call on Friday isn't blocked. High-level asks below, then a linked inventory (attached).

Top questions:
- ISO 27001 scope: confirm whether the service boundary is "Inference runtime + control plane" only, or if we must include managed integrations (partner storage) as in-scope in the Statement of Applicability.
- FedRAMP path: are we targeting FedRAMP Ready / P-ATO or a FedRAMP-tailored assessment? Does the current continuous monitoring plan meet the 90-day reporting expectations?
- Evidence windows: auditors want a typical "sample window" for logs, config snapshots, and change-control artifacts. Recommend we propose 90/180/365 windows per control class — need owners to confirm.
- Third-party attestations: which downstream vendors have SOC 2/ISO attestations we can reference? Any gaps where we'd need compensating controls?
- Key management: confirm HSM/KMS attestations and key rotation cadence for production secrets.

Immediate asks (for Friday):
1) Markus — can you confirm boundary and any outstanding network architecture diagrams by EOD Thursday?
2) Grace — can you propose a sampling matrix (logs/configs/patch evidence) and list of control owners for each sample bucket by Thursday?
3) Everyone — review the attached compliance_inventory_v0.7.xlsx and annotate missing artifacts inline.

Attachments: compliance_inventory_v0.7.xlsx (stub)

Thanks — Priya

--
Priya Natarajan
Head of Compliance Programs, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0131

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Adams <claire@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 10:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Compliance lighthouse: pre-audit questions & FedRAMP path

Thanks Priya — quick answers inline.

- Scope: Confirmed that the core in-scope boundary is the Redwood inference runtime (model serving + control plane) and our managed telemetry collectors. Partner-managed storage (S3 buckets owned by partners) remain out-of-scope unless we take custody of customer data. I'll attach an updated control_boundary_draft.pdf.

- FedRAMP: we're aiming for FedRAMP Ready initially (to position for later P-ATO). The current continuous monitoring pipeline covers log aggregation and alerting, but we lack automated integrity checks for configuration drift and formalized 90-day attestation reports. That is a gap and will need a 90-day remediation sprint and a process owner for continuous monitoring.

- Third-party attestations: list below (high level):
  * KMS vendor — SOC 2 Type II available (we use managed keys, not HSM-backed keys in every region).
  * CDN partner — ISO/PCI attestations, but smaller contract regionally.
  * Observability vendor — SOC 2 Type II, logs redaction controls documented.

Action: I'll circulate control_boundary_draft.pdf and a short owner list by EOD Thursday.

Subject: Re: Compliance lighthouse: pre-audit questions & FedRAMP path

Adding detail on evidence sampling and operational asks.

Evidence sampling recommendations (proposed):
- Logs: provide rolling 90-day log window for high-severity detection controls; 365 days for access control/authentication events.
- Config snapshots: retain daily snapshots for 30 days plus weekly snapshots for 12 months for infra-as-code artifacts.
- Change-control artifacts: use PR merge records + deployment manifests; propose 180-day window for patching and change tickets when demonstrating remediation timelines.
- Snapshot extraction: auditors will want deterministic snapshot times — we should provide one pre-audit golden snapshot and windowed extractions.

Owners (first pass):
- Logging & retention: Paul (observability) — I'll loop him for evidence pulls.
- Config drift & snapshots: Markus (infra)
- Change-control artifacts & tickets: SRE team leads (I'll provide names in the next note)

Scheduling: I recommend a 60-minute workshop with auditors and our owners to walk the boundary and sampling approach. Proposed slots: Thu May 14 10:00-11:00 PT or Thu May 14 15:00-16:00 PT. Please confirm availability so I can book.

Attachment: evidence_sampling_matrix.csv (skeleton)

From: Claire Adams <claire@acme.com>

Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Compliance lighthouse: pre-audit questions & FedRAMP path

Thanks — helpful. Auditor intake team at ISO Assess reviewed the initial attachments and can confirm the following:

- FedRAMP: targeting FedRAMP Ready makes sense as a staged approach. The auditors will want a documented 90-day continuous monitoring cadence and evidence of automated collection. They can accept a remediation plan if the sprint is time-boxed and owners are assigned.
- ISO 27001: for the Statement of Applicability, auditors prefer the conservative approach — include managed integrations in scope if we process customer-identifiable telemetry through them, otherwise document the explicit boundary exclusions.
- Sampling workshop: Thu May 14 15:00-16:00 PT works for the audit team; they will invite two technical reviewers.

Next steps for Redwood (requested by auditors):
1) Finalize control_boundary_draft.pdf and post to the shared drive (link preferred).
2) Provide the evidence_sampling_matrix.csv with owner names and example artifact IDs before the workshop.
3) Share a short continuous-monitoring remediation plan (<= 2 pages) that covers: gap description, owner, sprint timeline, and validation checks.

I will send a calendar invite for Thu May 14 15:00 PT and include the intake reviewers. Also attaching intake contact and auditor checklist on our side (note: we only included an intake stub in this thread).

Claire Adams
Senior Security Program Manager, Acme Financial Services
claire@acme.com
